claim: Conductance-based models of neural activity produce large amounts of data that can be hard to visualize and interpret.
source: Conductance-based models of neural activity produce large amounts of data that can be hard to visualize and interpret.
evidence: This is a statement about the nature of conductance-based models presented in the abstract.

claim: Neurons and circuits with similar behaviors can have very different values of the conductances that control intrinsic excitability and synaptic strength.
source: Experimental and computational studies have clearly demonstrated that neurons and circuits with similar behaviors can, nonetheless, have very different values of the conductances that control intrinsic excitability and synaptic strength.
evidence: This claim is supported by references to experimental and computational studies mentioned in the introduction.

claim: Prinz et al. (2004) showed that similar network activity can arise from widely different sets of membrane and synaptic conductances using a model of the crustacean stomatogastric ganglion (STG).
source: Using a model of the crustacean stomatogastric ganglion (STG), Prinz et al. (2004) showed that similar network activity can arise from widely different sets of membrane and synaptic conductances.
evidence: This claim is directly supported by citation to Prinz et al. (2004).

claim: Recent experimental measurements have shown two- to six-fold variability in individual components in the same identified neurons.
source: Recent experimental measurements have shown two- to six-fold variability in individual components in the same identified neurons (Schulz et al., 2006; Schulz et al., 2007; Roffman et al., 2012; Swensen and Bean, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies.

claim: RNA sequencing and other molecular measurements have shown significant cell-to-cell variability in the expression of ion channels.
source: The use of RNA sequencing and other molecular measurements have shown significant cell-to-cell variability in the expression of ion channels (Temporal et al., 2012; Temporal et al., 2014; Tobin et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to molecular measurement studies.

claim: Similar activities arise from different cellular and network mechanisms.
source: Together these results suggest that similar activities arise from different cellular and network mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited experimental results.

claim: Canonical models that capture the mean behavior of a set of observations are not sufficient to address issues of intrinsic variability.
source: Because of the intrinsic variability, canonical models that capture the mean behavior of a set of observations are not sufficient to address these issues (Golowasch et al., 2002; Balachandar and Prescott, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Prinz et al. (2004) introduced an ensemble modeling approach to incorporate intrinsic biophysical variability.
source: To incorporate intrinsic biophysical variability Prinz et al. (2004) introduced an ensemble modeling approach.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Prinz et al. (2004).

claim: Achard and De Schutter (2006) combined evolutionary strategies with a fitness function based on phase-plane analysis to find parameters that reproduce complex features in electrophysiological recordings.
source: An alternative was used by Achard and De Schutter (2006). They combined evolutionary strategies with a fitness function based on a phase-plane analysis of the models' solutions to find parameters that reproduce complex features in electrophysiological recordings of neuronal activity, and applied their procedure to obtain 20 very different computational models of cerebellar Purkinje cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Achard and De Schutter (2006).

claim: The authors adopt an approach similar to Achard and De Schutter (2006) and apply evolutionary techniques to optimize a different family of landscape functions.
source: Here, we adopt a similar approach and apply evolutionary techniques to optimize a different family of landscape functions that rely on thresholds or Poincaré sections to characterize the models' solutions.
evidence: This is a statement of the authors' methodological approach.

claim: Computational models allow inspection of how all components interact, which can be used to develop intuitions and predictions about how systems will respond to perturbations.
source: In contrast, computational models allow us to inspect how all the components interact and this can be used to develop intuitions and predictions about how these systems will respond to perturbations.
evidence: This is a general statement about the advantages of computational models.

claim: Much modeling work focuses on variables that are routinely measured in experiments, such as the membrane potential.
source: Despite this, much modeling work focuses on the variables of the models that are routinely measured in experiments, such as the membrane potential.
evidence: This is an observation about common practice in modeling work.

claim: Information about all state variables in models can be hard to represent when many conductances are at play.
source: While in the models we have access to all state variables, this information can be hard to represent when many conductances are at play.
evidence: This is a statement about the challenges of representing model data.

claim: The authors represent currents in a model neuron using stacked area plots showing the percent contribution of each current to the total current through the membrane at each time step.
source: We represent the currents in a model neuron using stacked area plots: at each time step, we display the shared contribution of each current to the total current through the membrane.
evidence: This is a description of the authors' visualization method.

claim: The stacked area plot representation is useful to visualize which currents are most important at each instant.
source: This representation is useful to visualize which currents are most important at each instant and allows the development of insight into how these currents behave when the system is perturbed.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the visualization method.

claim: The authors developed a novel representation based on computing the probability of V(t) to visualize changes in waveform as perturbations are applied.
source: Additionally, we developed a novel representation that relies on computing the probability of V⁢(t), which allows a visualization of these changes.
evidence: This is a description of another visualization method developed by the authors.

claim: The model neuron used in this work was described previously by Liu et al. (1998), Goldman et al. (2001), Prinz et al. (2004), and O'Leary et al. (2014).
source: In this work, we started with a well-studied model of neural activity described previously (Liu et al., 1998; Goldman et al., 2001; Prinz et al., 2004; O'Leary et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The neuron is modeled according to the Hodgkin-Huxley formalism using a single compartment with eight currents.
source: The neuron is modeled according to the Hodgkin-Huxley formalism using a single compartment with eight currents.
evidence: This is a description of the model structure.

claim: The procedure for landscape optimization consists of three steps: generating voltage traces by integration, scoring traces using an objective function, and attempting to find minima of the objective function.
source: The procedure consists of three steps. First, we generate voltage traces by integration of Equation 5 (Materials and methods). We then score the traces using an objective or landscape function that defines a target activity. Finally, we attempt to find minima of the objective function.
evidence: This is a description of the authors' optimization procedure.

claim: The authors chose measures that require little computing power but are sufficient to build successful target functions.
source: The procedure is efficient in part because we chose measures that require little computing power and yet are sufficient to build successful target functions.
evidence: This is a statement about the design choices in the optimization procedure.

claim: The authors avoid the use of Spike Density Functions (SDF) and Fourier transforms when estimating burst frequencies and burst durations.
source: For example, we avoid the use of Spike Density Functions (SDF) and Fourier transforms when estimating burst frequencies and burst durations.
evidence: This is a statement about methodological choices.

claim: At any given time stamp, the total inward and outward currents can be computed and the values of each current can be expressed as a percentage of this quantity.
source: At any given time stamp, we can compute the total inward and outward currents. We can then express the values of each current as a percentage of this quantity.
evidence: This is a description of the currentscape calculation method.

claim: The normalized values of the currents at any time can be displayed as a pie chart representing the share of each current type.
source: The normalized values of the currents at any time can be displayed as a pie chart representing the share of each current type (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a description of the visualization method shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The currentscapes are constructed by applying the normalization procedure to all time stamps and stacking the bars.
source: Because we want to observe how these percentages change in time, we display the shares in a bar instead of a disk. The currentscapes are constructed by applying this procedure to all time stamps and stacking the bars.
evidence: This is a description of how currentscapes are constructed.

claim: Six models that display similar membrane activity via different current compositions were selected for further study.
source: Based on this, we selected six models that display similar membrane activity via different current compositions for further study.
evidence: This is a description of the model selection process.

claim: The relationship between the dynamics of a given current type and the value of its maximal conductance is non-trivial because the models are nonlinear.
source: Because the models are nonlinear, the relationship between the dynamics of a given current type and the value of its maximal conductance is non-trivial.
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of nonlinear models.

claim: It can be difficult to predict the currentscapes based on the values of the maximal conductances.
source: It can be difficult to predict the currentscapes based on the values of the maximal conductances.
evidence: This is an observation about the complexity of the relationship between parameters and dynamics.

claim: In most cases, it appears that the larger the value of the maximal conductance, the larger the contribution of the corresponding current.
source: In most cases, it appears that the larger the value of the maximal conductance, the larger the contribution of the corresponding current.
evidence: This is a general observation from the data.

claim: The general relationship between maximal conductance and current contribution does not hold in all cases.
source: However, this does not hold in all cases.
evidence: This is an observation of exceptions to the general pattern.

claim: The ISI distributions exhibit complicated dependences on the control parameter that result in patterns reminiscent of classical period doubling routes to chaos.
source: The ISI distributions exhibit complicated dependences on the control parameter that result in beautiful patterns. For some current values, the cells produce small sets of ISI values indicating that the activity is periodic. However, this activity is quite different across regions. Interspersed with the regions of periodicity there are regions where the ISI distributions densely cover a band of values indicating non-periodic activity. Overall the patterns feature nested forking structures that are reminiscent of classical period doubling routes to chaos (Feigenbaum, 1978; Canavier et al., 1990).
evidence: This is an observation from Figure 6 with reference to classical dynamical systems theory.

claim: Models (d), (e) and (f) become tonic spikers when gCaT → 0.7 gCaT, but their frequencies are different.
source: Models (d), (e) and (f) become tonic spikers at this condition, but their frequencies are different.
evidence: This is an observation from Figure 7.

claim: In model (e), the spiking activity is not regular and the ISIs take several different values when gCaT → 0.7 gCaT.
source: Note that in the case of model (e) the spiking activity is not regular and the ISIs take several different values.
evidence: This is an observation from Figure 7.

claim: Decreasing any conductance can trigger qualitative changes in the waveform of the membrane potential and in the contributions of each current to the activity.
source: Decreasing any conductance can trigger qualitative changes in the waveform of the membrane potential and in the contributions of each current to the activity.
evidence: This is a general observation from the perturbation experiments.

claim: There are ranges of conductance values where a small change results in a smooth deformation of the waveform, and there are specific values at which abrupt transitions take place.
source: Overall, these plots show that for any given current, there are ranges of the conductance values where a small change results in a smooth deformation of the waveform, and there are specific values at which abrupt transitions take place.
evidence: This is an observation from Figures 12 and 13.

claim: Model (f) is less resilient to CaT perturbation than model (a), and the transition to tonic spiking takes place at lower conductance values.
source: Model (f) is less resilient to this perturbation and this transition takes place at lower conductance values.
evidence: This is a comparative observation from Figure 12.

claim: Model (c) is less resilient to CaS perturbation since it becomes quiescent for lower decrements of the maximal conductance than the other models.
source: Model (c) is less resilient to this perturbation since it becomes quiescent for lower decrements of the maximal conductance than the other models.
evidence: This is an observation from Figure 12.

claim: The activity termed plateau oscillations was reported in models of leech heart interneurons and in experiments in lamprey spinal neurons.
source: This type of activity is termed plateau oscillations and was reported in models of leech heart interneurons (Cymbalyuk and Calabrese, 2000) and in experiments in lamprey spinal neurons (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: While the effect of removing a current on that same current is relatively predictable, the rest of the currents become rearranged in complicated ways.
source: Notice that while the effect of removing a current on that same current (diagonal panels) is relatively predictable, the rest of the currents become rearranged in complicated ways.
evidence: This is an observation from Figure 15.

claim: There is an ever larger availability of experimental data to inform detailed models of identified neuron types.
source: There is an ever larger availability of experimental data to inform detailed models of identified neuron types (McDougal et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation.

claim: Experimenters have determined the kinetics of many channel types, both in vertebrate and invertebrate neurons.
source: Experimenters have determined the kinetics of many channel types, both in vertebrate and invertebrate neurons.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of experimental knowledge.

claim: There are model databases with thousands of parameters which permit the development of large scale models of neural tissue.
source: There are also model databases with thousands of parameters which permit the development of large scale models of neural tissue (Bezaire et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation.

claim: One difficulty in ensemble modeling is the necessity of incorporating biological variability observed in parameters while requiring models to capture target activity.
source: One difficulty in ensemble modeling is the necessity of incorporating the biological variability observed in some of the parameters – such as the conductances – at the same time that we require the models to capture some target activity.
evidence: This is a statement about challenges in modeling.

claim: The database approach has the advantage that it provides a notion of how likely it is to find conductances within a search range that will produce the activity.
source: One advantage of this approach is that it provides a notion of how likely it is to find conductances within a search range that will produce the activity.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the database approach.

claim: The landscape approach has the advantage that it can be scaled to include large numbers of parameters.
source: This approach has the advantage that it can be scaled to include large numbers of parameters.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the landscape approach.

claim: If a particular solution is interesting, genetic algorithms can be used on successful target functions to 'breed' as many closely related models as desired.
source: Additionally, if a particular solution is interesting, we can use genetic algorithms on successful target functions to 'breed' as many closely related models as desired.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of the landscape approach.

claim: A successful target function can determine if a random perturbation results in disruption of the activity and this can be used to perform population-based sensitivity analyses.
source: A successful target function can determine if a random perturbation results in disruption of the activity and this can be used to perform population-based sensitivity analyses (Devenyi and Sobie, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation.

claim: Different modeling problems require different target functions.
source: Different modeling problems require different target functions (Roemschied et al., 2014; Fox et al., 2017; Migliore et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.

claim: One challenge in target function design is that sometimes we do not know a priori if the model contains solutions that will produce good minima.
source: one challenge in their design is that sometimes we do not know a priori if the model contains solutions that will produce good minima.
evidence: This is a statement about challenges in optimization.

claim: A poorly constrained target function can feature multiple local minima that could make the optimization harder.
source: In addition, a poorly constrained target function can feature multiple local minima that could make the optimization harder, so even if there are good minima they may be hard to find.
evidence: This is a statement about challenges in optimization.

claim: One difference between the landscape functions in Achard and De Schutter (2006) and the ones utilized in this work is that their setup compares model solutions to a target time series via a phase-plane method.
source: One difference between the landscape functions in Achard and De Schutter (2006) and the ones utilized here is that in their setup model solutions are compared to a target time series via a phase-plane method.
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work.

claim: The functions introduced in this work use an analysis based on Poincaré sections or thresholds to characterize the waveform and to define an error or score.
source: The functions introduced in this work use an analysis based on Poincaré sections or thresholds to characterize the waveform and to define an error or score.
evidence: This is a description of the authors' methodological approach.

claim: The authors' approach is successful in finding hundreds of models that display a target activity in minutes using a commercially available desktop computer.
source: Our approach is successful in finding hundreds of models that display a target activity in minutes using a commercially available desktop computer.
evidence: This is a statement about the performance of the authors' method.

claim: Application of evolutionary techniques to optimize these functions provides a natural means to model the intrinsic variability observed in biological populations.
source: Application of evolutionary techniques to optimize these functions provides a natural means to model the intrinsic variability observed in biological populations.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the approach.

claim: Once a behavior of interest is successfully captured, computational models possess a mechanistic description of the phenomena that can be used to test ideas and inform experiments.
source: One of the main benefits of computational modeling is that once a behavior of interest is successfully captured we then possess a mechanistic description of the phenomena that can be used to test ideas and inform experiments (Coggan et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2016; Devenyi and Sobie, 2016; Gong and Sobie, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.

claim: As models gain biophysical detail, their advantages wane in the face of the complexity imposed by larger numbers of variables and parameters.
source: As the models gain biophysical detail these advantages wane in the face of the complexity imposed by larger numbers of variables and parameters.
evidence: This is a statement about the challenges of detailed models.

claim: The development of novel visualization procedures has the potential to assist intuition into the details of how these models work.
source: The development of novel visualization procedures has the potential to assist intuition into the details of how these models work (Gutierrez et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation.

claim: The currentscape representation is easily generalizable to multi-compartment models and small networks, and to any type of electrically excitable cell, such as models of cardiac cells.
source: Our representation is simple and displays in a concise way the contribution of each current to the activity. This representation is easily generalizable to multi-compartment models and small networks, and to any type of electrically excitable cell, such as models of cardiac cells (Britton et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the generalizability of the method with citation support.

claim: The responses of the models to current injections and gradual decrements of their conductances can be diverse and complex.
source: The responses of the models to current injections and gradual decrements of their conductances can be diverse and complex.
evidence: This is a summary observation from the results.

claim: Inspection of the ISI distributions revealed wide ranges of parameter values for which the activity appears irregular.
source: Inspection of the ISI distributions revealed wide ranges of parameter values for which the activity appears irregular, and similar regimes can be attained by gradually removing some of the currents.
evidence: This is an observation from the ISI distribution analysis.

claim: Period doubling routes to chaos in neurons have been observed experimentally and in conductance-based models.
source: Period doubling routes to chaos in neurons have been observed experimentally and in conductance-based models (Hayashi et al., 1982; Hayashi and Ishizuka, 1992; Szücs et al., 2001; Canavier et al., 1990; Xu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to experimental and modeling studies.

claim: The sort of bifurcation diagrams displayed by these models upon current injection are qualitatively similar to those exhibited by simplified models of spiking neurons for which further theoretical insight is possible.
source: The sort of bifurcation diagrams displayed by these models upon current injection are qualitatively similar to those exhibited by simplified models of spiking neurons for which further theoretical insight is possible (Touboul and Brette, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation.

claim: Period doubling bifurcations and low dimensional chaos arise repeatedly in neural models of different natures including rate models.
source: Period doubling bifurcations and low dimensional chaos arise repeatedly in neural models of different natures including rate models (Ermentrout, 1984; Alonso, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.

claim: The bursters studied here are close (in parameter space) to aperiodic or irregular regimes suggesting that such regimes are ubiquitous and not special cases.
source: The bursters studied here are close (in parameter space) to aperiodic or irregular regimes suggesting that such regimes are ubiquitous and not special cases.
evidence: This is an inference from the results.

claim: Similar membrane activities can be attained by multiple mechanisms that correspond to different current compositions in these model neurons.
source: We showed that in these model neurons similar membrane activities can be attained by multiple mechanisms that correspond to different current compositions.
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding.

claim: Because the dynamical mechanisms driving the activity are different in different models, perturbations can result in qualitatively different scenarios.
source: Because the dynamical mechanisms driving the activity are different in different models, perturbations can result in qualitatively different scenarios.
evidence: This is an inference from the results.

claim: The visualization methods allow gathering intuition on how different the responses can be and to explore the contribution of each current type to the neural activity.
source: Our visualization methods allow us to gather intuition on how different these responses can be and to explore the contribution of each current type to the neural activity.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the visualization methods.

claim: The response to perturbations of a population can be diverse and hard to describe even in the case of single compartment bursters.
source: Even in the case of single compartment bursters, the response to perturbations of a population can be diverse and hard to describe.
evidence: This is an observation about the complexity of the results.

claim: The models respond to perturbations in different ways, but there are also similarities among their responses.
source: This representation shows that the models respond to perturbations in different ways, but that there are also similarities among their responses.
evidence: This is a summary observation from the results.

claim: A concise representation of the effect of a perturbation is a necessary step towards developing a classification scheme for the responses.
source: A concise representation of the effect of a perturbation is a necessary step towards developing a classification scheme for the responses.
evidence: This is a statement about future directions.

claim: The kinetic equations describing the seven voltage-gated conductances were modeled as in Liu et al. (1998).
source: The kinetic equations describing the seven voltage-gated conductances were modeled as in Liu et al. (1998)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation.

claim: For some values of the parameters, the system can display multistability.
source: For some values of the parameters, the system (Equation 5) can display multistability (Cymbalyuk et al., 2002; Shilnikov et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.
